messages:
maria-cs: FYI received a ticket — customer sees duplicated full generations when their client reconnects after an SSE drop. They claim two billed completions for the same user action. request_id: r-41c2f9a0

aj-engr: Can you paste the logs or the exact sequence they saw? Is this over our hosted API or Dedicated?

maria-cs: Hosted. Customer captured client logs + server events. Short sequence they gave: connect -> stream started -> network blip -> client reconnects without resume_token -> server returns a fresh completion -> then client resumes and gets leftover chunks from first run, so two outputs in UI. They attached a screenshot of two messages.

dan-oncall: Do we have the server-side timeline for r-41c2f9a0? I can pull traces. Suspect resume semantics didn't clear outstanding KV cache or we treated reconnect as new stream and later replayed prior partials.

sara-ml: Important to know whether the client attempted a resume header (Resume-Token) or used Idempotency-Key. If no idempotency key, reconnect could be interpreted as a new request.

maria-cs: Customer says they attempted a resume_token but it was stale; client fell back to new request without idempotency. They pasted client code snippet: ```js
const evt = new EventSource(url);
evt.onopen = () => console.log('open');
evt.onmessage = (m) => render(m.data);
// onclose -> try reconnect with previous resume_token header if 410 then start new request
```

tom-sde: Can you share the server trace? I pulled r-41c2f9a0 span: 
```
[2026-04-01T12:01:39Z] recv stream start (session s-88a)
[2026-04-01T12:01:42Z] partials emitted: token_range 0-87
[2026-04-01T12:01:44Z] connection lost (client TCP FIN)
[2026-04-01T12:01:44Z] session state preserved (s-88a), resume window open until +10s
[2026-04-01T12:01:55Z] new connection without resume header -> allocated new session s-88b -> started new generation (g-992)
[2026-04-01T12:02:02Z] later client POSTed resume_token but server considered it for s-88a and re-emitted leftover chunks to client id p-77
```

sara-ml: That timeline matches a race: client reconnected after the resume window expiry, new gen created, later resume attempt caused replay. This is classic non-idempotent retry + late resume.

aj-engr: Two possible mitigations here: 1) require/strongly recommend Idempotency-Key for clients that may do fallback-to-new-request behavior, 2) make resume idempotent by rejecting resume tokens once a new generation was created for same user action.

maria-cs: Customer is upset because they were billed twice. Billing system billed both g-991 and g-992 (partial+full). billing-bot, can we check whether we can refund the duplicated token usage for r-41c2f9a0?

billing-bot: Invoice check done. Both generations consumed compute units; policy allows manual credit for confirmed duplicate-generation due to reconnect race. Need approval from finance.

dan-oncall: For immediate customer mitigation we can: - issue a manual credit - provide recommended client pattern (use Idempotency-Key + only fallback-to-new when resume returns explicit 410) - increase resume window slightly for edge clients. Which should we do first?

maria-cs: Customer accepts manual credit + client guidance. They asked for repro steps we can run to validate fix. Can eng provide minimal repro script?

tom-sde: I'll sketch a repro using curl + SSE proxy. Steps: 1) start streaming request with resume capability and idempotency off 2) after N tokens, kill TCP connection 3) immediately open new connection without resume header (simulate fallback) 4) then send stale resume header and observe second emission. Example curl sequence: ```bash
# start stream (server issues resume_token in header X-Resume-Token)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=xyz" > part1.txt &
# kill after a few seconds
kill $!
# open new stream without resume
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=xyz" > full.txt &
# later attempt resume (stale token)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Resume-Token: s-88a" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=xyz" > replay.txt
```

sara-ml: For a durable fix we should treat resume attempts after a new generation as a no-op (respond 409) instead of replaying leftover chunks. That avoids duplicate emission. Also, adjust billing to not count replayed leftover emissions if they are flagged as 'replay_of' in telemetry.

aj-engr: Agree. Implementation plan: A) server marks resume_token as consumed when a new gen starts for same logical request B) change resume path to check resume_token generation mapping and return 409 if mapping is stale C) add telemetry flag so billing can detect replayed generations and auto-exempt. I'll open a small PR.

maria-cs: Meanwhile I've created a ticket for finance credit and sent recommended client guidance to customer (Idempotency-Key + explicit 410 handling). They asked for ETA on server change.

dan-oncall: tom/sara/aj — can we get a patch to prod-fix timeline? If low-risk, hotfix in 48-72h, otherwise next sprint.

tom-sde: I'll scope the change. Likely small: ~2 files in resume controller + tests. If approvals go quick, target 48h.

aj-engr: I'll add tests for race case and update docs to warn about fallback behavior.

maria-cs: Thanks team. I'll update customer that we issued a temporary credit and will deploy a server-side mitigation in ~48-72h, plus client guidance. Closing loop after PR. :thumbsup:
